evidence.requirements: Met: the start page has the 'Cartridges' heading, links whose text is exactly the record name, the Search and Family controls, and the '<n> cartridges' count (index.html:16-29, catalog.js:34-41, list.jpg). The detail view has the facts, the water capacity with its source link, grouped Symbol/Value/Unit tables, a Print button and an 'All cartridges' link (app.js:113-191, detail-308_win.jpg). Each detail view has its own hash address that survives a reload (catalog.js:58-71). The SVG has role=img and aria-label '<name> drawing' (drawing.js:342). The required dimension set L1/L2/L3/L6/R1/R/P1/P2/H1/H2/G1/E1/α is drawn (drawing.js:181-235). Tolerances sit inline, e.g. 'L1 39.62 -0.2' and the list's '19.15 -0.25 mm'. Print fits one A4 page (print-308_win.jpg). There are no dependencies and the app works from file://. Partly met: (1) 'Labels do not overlap': the α label sits on the dash-dot centre line in every bottleneck view (detail-308_win.jpg, detail-9_3_x_74_r.jpg). The 9 mm 'L3 19.15 -0.25' label is wider than its span and is crossed by the head-face extension line (detail-9_mm_luger.jpg). The R labels are cut by their own extension lines (drawing.js:202-204, which ends the extension at row+1 while the label top is row+0.63; visible in detail-9_3_x_74_r.jpg and detail-44_rem_mag.jpg). The rotated diameter labels are crossed by neighbouring horizontal extension lines. (2) The title block says 'Scale 1:1' (drawing.js:319), but the SVG is stretched to the container width on screen and in print, so the stated scale is false. (3) The α angle is drawn as a 4.5 mm arc at the virtual cone apex, inside the bullet, with no construction lines (drawing.js:287-295), so it does not visibly dimension the shoulder. (4) The outside view leaves out the mouth face between H2/2 and G1/2: the case path ends at (L3, H2/2) and the bullet path starts at (L3, G1/2) (geometry.js:224, 284). (5) The print page has no separate running header or footer; the h1 and an end-of-content footer stand in for them.
evidence.correctness: The geometry follows the rules closely. The chamfer uses min(f·tanβ, R1/4) (geometry.js:421). The rimfire half-round has radius min(R/2,(R1-P1)/2) with its outermost point at R1/2 (geometry.js:174-185). The groove floor and ramp follow the rule, and the belt ramp uses dz = dr/tan δ (geometry.js:209-217). The shoulder runs through (P2/2,L1)-(H1/2,L2) with r1 min/r2 fillets. The ogive ρ formula and centre are correct and reach the meplat exactly at L6 (geometry.js:339-345). The seating/k table matches the brief (geometry.js:304-329). The heeled 22 LR uses H2 for the exposed part and H2-2tb for the heel. Walls, w and the primer pocket table are correct (geometry.js:410-451). Proportions match the references: the 308, 300 WM, 9 mm and 22 LR outlines are comparable in aspect and shoulder position. Values and angles are formatted as published ('1°45'00"', '4150'). Problems: the false 'Scale 1:1'. The α arc sits at the apex in the bullet and is disconnected from the shoulder. The diameter extension lines run the full length of the case at r = P1/2 and E1/2 and lie almost on top of the body outline, which doubles the edges and hides the taper (detail-9_mm_luger.jpg, detail-308_win.jpg). The mouth face is missing in the outside view. On straight cases the wall tapers from tb to tn over the whole body, an interpretation the brief does not state. Hatching is hardly visible in the 0.6 mm walls. Print is one page (print-308_win.jpg, e2e/app.test.js:156-169).
evidence.security: No innerHTML anywhere. The DOM is built with createElement and text nodes (app.js:40-47). The SVG string escapes every text and the aria-label through escapeXml (drawing.js:342, 357-365, 372-374) and is parsed with DOMParser. There is no eval or Function. There are no external requests apart from user-clicked source links; e2e/app.test.js:130-141 asserts that only file: requests are made.
evidence.code_quality: Clear module split: format, catalog, geometry, drawing and app, as UMD-style IIFEs that work from file:// and in Node. Functions are well named and the constants are documented (drawing.js:12-38). The model reports missing values as notes. Small blemishes: unused destructured variables in buildScene (format, geometry, junctionCone at drawing.js:158-160); TOLERANCE_SUFFIX declared after the function that uses it (format.js:106); a mix of cp.caseHead and head. Size suits the task (about 1,250 lines of source).
evidence.tests: The unit tests check concrete rule values: the rim classification thresholds, the 223 chamfer/groove/body-start points, the belt ramp at δ, seating depths, the meplat, ogive tangency, the heeled radii, tn/tb/w, the pocket sizes, the monotone profile and simple section polygons (geometry.test.js). They also check formatting of symbols, units, angles and tolerances (format.test.js). drawing.test.js checks label overlap against labels and outline for all 25 records, but not against extension, dimension or centre lines, which is why the visible overlaps get through. The e2e tests cover search, filter, routing and reload, the facts and tables, no network, the phone width, one-page print and dark mode (e2e/app.test.js). There is no test of the rimfire half-round, of the shoulder passing through the published points at angle α, or of the mouth face.
evidence.ux_design: The facts and tables are dense and calm, in a two-column grid with monospaced values (detail-308_win.jpg). The drawing is weaker. The right-hand diameter columns are packed, and horizontal extension lines cross the rotated labels. The α label lies on the centre line. The title block is oversized: on 22 LR and 44 Mag its text is larger than the drawing labels and it takes almost half the figure (detail-22_long_rifle.jpg). In print the label halo is turned off (styles.css:469-471), so lines run through the text (print-308_win.jpg 'H1 8.72'). The print layout itself is compact, but the dt labels in the facts grid come out larger than their values. Dark mode exists in CSS, but no dark screenshot was provided.
evidence.accessibility: The SVG has role=img and an accessible name. All values are also in tables with th scope=col and scope=row (app.js:164-172). The inputs have label for (index.html:20-25). The count is announced through role=status aria-live. Focus moves to the h1 on route change (app.js:220). :focus-visible gives an outline. Contrast of ink-soft #4d545c on #fcfbf8 is about 7:1. There is no richer text description of the drawing beyond its name, and the 'Not drawn' notes list is the only text alternative for missing features.
evidence.simplicity: No runtime dependencies, no build. Six small script files and one CSS file; Playwright is the only dev dependency. The amount of code is proportionate to the drawing rules.
evidence.maintainability: The README gives the file map and the commands for install, unit tests and e2e tests (README.md). There is a package-lock.json. Missing: any CI pipeline, ADRs, specs or design notes explaining interpretations (for example the straight-case wall blend or the apex α arc); an engines field or .nvmrc for Node 22; any versioning or release approach beyond 'version 1.0.0'. Playwright uses a caret range, and installing the Playwright browser is a manual step that is only mentioned in passing.
evidence.visual_design: The palette is restrained, typography and tabular numerals are consistent, rules are thin and the uppercase micro-labels are tidy (list.jpg, detail views). Value columns do not line up from one table to the next because each table sizes its columns independently (detail-308_win.jpg: case head vs collar vs lengths). The drawing's line weights are fine, but the doubled edges from the extension lines and the giant title text make it look less finished than the tables.
evidence.layout: The hierarchy is sound: toolbar, name, facts, drawing, then the tables side by side, and the list is clean with nothing clipped (list.jpg). On short cartridges (22 LR, 9 mm, 44 Mag) the drawing fills only about 70% of the figure width, because the 74 mm minimum title block sets the width, and the title block dominates. The print page fits on one page with a 4-column table flow and spare space at the bottom (print-308_win.jpg).
evidence.usability: Live search with alternative names, a family select, a result count, plain links to detail pages, a back link, a Print button and a not-found view (index.html:61-64). Few steps for every task. The drawing's clutter on the right side makes values slower to read, though they are all in the tables as well.
evidence.reception: Reloaders and engineers would trust the data tables and the correct formatting. The drawing is recognisably right in outline, but the stated 'Scale 1:1', the disconnected α arc, the labels struck through by lines and the doubled body edges would draw criticism from a drafting-literate audience. Many would use it as a reference, though few would recommend it for its drawings.

unmet_requirements: Labels overlap lines: the α label on the centre line, the 9 mm L3 label crossed by the head extension line, the R labels cut by their extension lines, and rotated diameter labels crossed by extension lines (lines show through the text in print).
The title block says 'Scale 1:1', but the drawing is scaled to the container width on screen and in print.
The shoulder angle α is drawn as a small arc at the virtual cone apex inside the bullet, without construction lines, so it does not clearly dimension the shoulder.
The mouth face is missing in the outside view: there is no line between H2/2 and G1/2 at L3.
Print has no separate page header or footer; the h1 and the end-of-content source block stand in for them.
strengths: The geometry rules are implemented faithfully and documented: chamfer, rimfire half-round, groove and belt ramp at δ, fillets, the tangent ogive with the exact ρ, the seating/k table, the heeled bullet, walls, w and primer pockets, with unit tests on concrete values.
Data presentation is correct and secure: tolerances inline, angles in D°M'S", symbols and units as specified, no innerHTML, escaped SVG text, and no network requests (checked in e2e).
Simple, dependency-free architecture that runs from file://, with hash routing, live search over alternative names, and an e2e suite that checks one-page A4 print, phone width and dark mode.
issues: Drawing legibility: diameter extension lines run the full case length on top of the body outline, the α label sits on the centre line, and labels are crossed by extension lines, which is worse in print where the halo is removed. The overlap test ignores these lines.

Wrong or unclear drafting information: 'Scale 1:1' is stated for a drawing scaled to fit, the α arc is placed at the cone apex away from the shoulder, and the mouth face is missing in the outside view.
Maintainability gaps: no CI, no ADRs or specs documenting interpretations, no pinned Node version or engines field, and no release approach.
review.verdict: The geometry engine, data formatting and list and detail flows are solid, well tested and secure, and the outlines match the reference drawings in proportion. The drawing's drafting quality (overlapping lines through labels, a false 1:1 scale, a disconnected α arc, oversized title block) and the missing CI and documentation mean it needs another pass before it goes to a technical audience.
